subject: SOC 2 Type II — midnight cutover / evidence inclusivity question
messages:
From: Nick Evans <nick.evans@auditpartner.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Samantha Li <sam.li@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 Type II — midnight cutover and EOD evidence inclusivity

Hi Rachel,

Quick follow on the evidence we requested for Acme's Feb–Oct coverage: we noticed the customer performed a production cutover that was logged at 2026-10-31T00:00:00Z (UTC). For the Type II procedures we need to understand whether events that occur exactly at 00:00:00 UTC on the first/last day are considered inside the prior reporting period or the new period.

Specifically please confirm:
- How Redwood defines the point-in-time "snapshot" cutoff (UTC vs local, ingest vs event timestamp).
- Whether your EOD backup that runs around midnight produces objects with event timestamps vs ingest timestamps.
- If partial-day coverage will be accepted, what supporting artifacts you can provide (manifest, S3 object timestamps, DB snapshot manifest, bridge letter).

We attached an updated evidence checklist (soc2_evidence_request_v2.pdf) with the exact items auditors will look for. Short timeline would be helpful — if you can confirm the cutoff definition and whether you can provide a manifest + bridge letter by EOD Tuesday that would keep the audit on schedule.

Thanks,
Nick Evans
Audit Partner — AuditPartner LLP
Attachments: soc2_evidence_request_v2.pdf

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nick Evans <nick.evans@auditpartner.com>
Cc: Samantha Li <sam.li@acme.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — midnight cutover and EOD evidence inclusivity

Hi Nick — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: we can provide explicit, ISO-8601 timestamps and object manifests that show ingest and event times; we want to be precise about the definition so the report wording is unambiguous. A couple of product-ops details below so we're all aligned.

What Redwood uses today:
- Canonical internal timestamps: we store events and logs in UTC.
- Ingest time vs event time: our logging pipeline records both (event_timestamp and ingest_timestamp). The ingest_timestamp is assigned when the log is accepted by our runtime; event_timestamp is whatever the source emitted.
- Backups & snapshots: nightly DB snapshots are initiated by orchestration at 23:59:50 local (customer region) but the snapshot manifest records the UTC completion timestamp.

For Acme's cutover: our records show the migration traffic switch was observed at 2026-10-31T00:00:00Z in event_timestamp and the snapshot completion was 2026-10-31T00:02:17Z ingest_timestamp.

Proposed approach to satisfy auditors: provide
1) Snapshot manifest with UTC completion timestamps for the relevant objects (S3 manifests + checksums).
2) A short bridge letter from Redwood stating we define the point-in-time cutoff as an inclusive instant (i.e. events with event_timestamp < 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z count toward the prior period) and specifying which field (event_timestamp) is authoritative for the snapshot.
3) Sample lines from the log_manifest showing both event_timestamp and ingest_timestamp for cutover events.

I'm attaching the cutover schedule and the customer-reported cutover times (cutover_schedule.xlsx). Karthik — can you confirm the exact manifest path and whether we can produce object-level checksums by tomorrow? If we can, Nick, we'll aim to send the manifest + bridge text for your review by EOD Tuesday.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Director, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: cutover_schedule.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — midnight cutover and EOD evidence inclusivity (technical)

Rachel / Grace — quick technical note from runtime/infra:

- Object manifests: we can export S3 manifest with object key, md5, size, and last_modified (UTC). Those last_modified values reflect when the snapshot object was written/closed by the backup job.
- Logs: the logging pipeline stores event_timestamp (producer) and ingest_timestamp (receiver). We can produce filtered log snippets for the window 2026-10-30T23:59:30Z → 2026-10-31T00:05:00Z including both timestamps.
- Snapshots sometimes finish slightly after cutoff (as in Rachel's example, completion at 00:02:17Z). For audit purposes, the manifest completion timestamp plus the log evidence that shows the final write and checksums is sufficient to demonstrate the capture point.

Actionable items I can deliver by EOD Tuesday:
- S3 snapshot manifest: s3://acme-backups/2026-10/manifest.json (we'll produce as CSV export).
- Log snippet export for the 5-minute window around cutover (with both timestamps).
- A one-paragraph bridge letter draft we can sign that defines the cutoff as inclusive of events with event_timestamp < 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z and references the manifest path + checksum file.

Note: we'll redact any PII in the log snippet but preserve timestamps and request IDs. If the auditor needs raw objects for hashing, we'll arrange secure transfer via the shared S3 bucket.

—Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: log_manifest_sample.txt

From: Nick Evans <nick.evans@auditpartner.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samantha Li <sam.li@acme.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — midnight cutover and EOD evidence inclusivity (acceptance & next steps)

Thanks Rachel / Karthik — that level of granularity is excellent and aligns with what we need. A few clarifications and next steps:

- Accepted definition: auditors will accept an inclusive cutoff defined by event_timestamp when supported by a manifest + log evidence showing both event_timestamp and ingest_timestamp. Please ensure the bridge letter explicitly names the cutoff instant (e.g., "events with event_timestamp earlier than 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z are covered by the prior period").
- Evidence checklist: manifest (object keys + checksums + UTC completion), 5-minute log snippet, and the bridge letter are sufficient for the cutover portion of the scope.
- Bridge letter: please use the attached template as a starting point and include the manifest path and checksum file name. We'll accept an emailed signed PDF or DocuSign via the link below.

If you can send the manifest CSV + draft bridge letter by EOD Tuesday we can incorporate into the Type II workpapers and avoid a delay.
